title: AI Bootcamp: Zero to Hero
rule: One lesson at a time. Take the time you need.
note: Your first lesson starts when you sign in.

sections.title: Foundations
sections.summary: Set up your AI and teach it your business, write in your voice, build brand guidelines, hand off the tasks you hate, re-engage dead leads, and keep a decision log.

sections.title: Clients and Social
sections.summary: Ask for reviews, plan your social media, and create your first posts.

sections.title: Calendar, Notes and Listings
sections.summary: Use your calendar, keep notes, stay in touch with past clients, and write listing descriptions.

sections.title: Letters and Offers
sections.summary: Write Letters of Opinion, read an offer, and track deal deadlines.

sections.title: Deal Card
sections.summary: Build deal cards and make your lead calls.

sections.title: Advanced
sections.summary: Prep listing paperwork and book showings.

sections.title: Your List

sections.title: Review
sections.summary: Review every lesson and write down your next step.

days.title: Pick Your AI and Tell It About Your Business
days.why: It can only help with a business it understands.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Pick one AI and start on the paid plan: Grok Bot or Claude Pro. My pick for real estate agents is Grok Bot.
Install it on your phone and your computer.

Explain your business: who you are, your experience, and everything it would need to know to help you. Examples: how many houses you have sold, what areas you like to work in, and the roadblocks and challenges where it could help you manage, fix, solve or add leverage.
Ask it to save what you set up today.
days.assignment: Done when it can play back a short summary of your business and you are happy it is accurate.
prompts: I'm a REALTOR® and I want you to understand my business. Ask me questions one at a time: how many houses I've sold, what areas I like to work in, how long I've been in real estate, and the roadblocks and challenges where you could help me manage, fix, solve or add leverage. When we're done, give me a short summary of my business and save it.
Save everything we set up today, so you remember it next time.

days.title: Teach It Your Writing Style
days.why: What you feed it is what it writes like.
days.minutes: 30 minutes to start, longer if you go deeper
days.tip: Talk instead of type. Use the microphone; it is faster and the draft is still yours to approve.
steps: Give it samples of writing you like: emails you have sent, articles, or authors. You can also just paste a link. If there is a blog writer you like, or a social media account whose captions you love, copy the URL and share it with your AI. With every link, tell it why you are sharing it and what you like about it, such as the tone, the short sentences, or how it opens. That way it learns not only what you like, but why.
Tell it your pet peeves too. Share everything you do not like in writing (for example em dashes, long paragraphs, salesy words) so it knows what to avoid.
Ask it to make up a mock scenario and draft an email to one of your clients.
Send it to yourself, or load it as a draft in Outlook or Gmail, so you see exactly how it writes.
Coach it and adjust anything that does not sound like you.
Every suggestion you make gets saved as your Email writing SOP (standard operating procedure). Rule one of the SOP: it drafts, you approve, nothing goes out until you say so.
Ask it to save what you set up today.
days.assignment: Done when the mock email sounds like you and every change you made is saved in your Email writing SOP.
prompts: Here are samples of writing I like, including links to writers and social media accounts whose style I love, and what I like about each one. Here are my pet peeves, the things I never want, such as em dashes. Learn my style. Then make up a mock scenario with one of my clients and draft an email to them. Send it only to me, or save it as a draft, so I can see it. I'll coach you on what to change. Every time I make a suggestion, save it to my Email writing SOP. Rule one: you draft, I approve, and nothing goes out until I say so.
Save everything we set up today, so you remember it next time.

days.title: Build Your Brand Guidelines
days.why: Every post and flyer should look like you without starting over each time.
days.minutes: 30 minutes to start, longer if you go deeper
steps: Pick the fonts you like.
Pick your colour palette.
Upload your headshots.
Upload any marketing materials you have already created.
Add the Faris Team logo.
Have your AI turn it all into one brand guidelines file and save it.
Before we close, list every decision we made in this chat and save them. I'll move them into my decision log once it's set up.
days.assignment: Done when your brand guidelines are saved and your AI can describe your fonts, colours and look back to you. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: I'm going to give you the fonts I like, my colour palette, my headshots, marketing materials I've made, and the Faris Team logo. Ask me anything you need, then create my brand guidelines: fonts, colours, photo style, logo use, and how my posts and materials should look. Save it so every marketing piece follows it.
Before we close, list every decision we made in this chat and save them. I'll move them into my decision log once it's set up.

days.title: Brain Dump the Tasks You Hate
days.why: Now that it knows your business and your style, it can help you decide what to hand off first. Everyone's list will be different.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Do a full brain dump of every task you hate doing. Do not filter it.
With your AI, rank the list from easiest to hardest.
Build a strategy together for how it will take these on, one at a time, starting with the easiest.
Stay on this list. Do not drift into other topics.
Ask it to save the ranked list and the strategy.
Before we close, list every decision we made in this chat and save them. I'll move them into my decision log once it's set up.
days.assignment: Done when your full list is ranked easiest to hardest, the strategy is saved, and the first (easiest) task is picked. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: I'm going to brain dump every task in my business I hate doing. Don't suggest anything until I say I'm done. Then help me rank them from easiest to hardest for you to take on. Build a strategy for how we'll work through them one at a time, starting with the easiest. Keep us on this list and don't drift into other topics. Save the ranked list and the strategy.
Before we close, list every decision we made in this chat and save them. I'll move them into my decision log once it's set up.

days.title: Re-Engage Your Dead Leads
days.why: Your database already has people who went quiet. The right message can restart the conversation.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Ask your AI to research ways to re-engage dead leads by text and by email, and the best practices for both.
Explain your situation: you have leads in your database who went quiet.
Give it a couple of examples (real or mock).

Create a skill (a saved set of steps your AI can repeat): you give it a person's details, it gives you 5 text options, or 5 email options if that is where they want to be met, to re-engage them into a conversation about buying or selling.
Ask it to save the skill.
Before we close, list every decision we made in this chat and save them. I'll move them into my decision log once it's set up.
days.assignment: Done when the re-engagement skill is saved and you have run it on one real dead lead and got 5 options back. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: Research the best ways to re-engage cold real estate leads by text and by email, and the best practices for each. Then I'll explain my situation and give you a couple of examples. Create a skill: when I give you a person's details, give me 5 text messages, or 5 email options if email is where they'd rather be reached, to restart a conversation about buying or selling. Don't send anything. I approve first.
Before we close, list every decision we made in this chat and save them. I'll move them into my decision log once it's set up.

days.title: Set Up Your Decision Log
days.why: A decision log gives your AI a memory, so you do not have to retrain it every time.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Choose where it lives: an Excel spreadsheet, Google Drive or Dropbox, however you see fit.
Have your AI set up the columns: date, area (for example email, texts, leads), the decision or SOP, and the reason.
Add everything from the earlier lessons: your business summary, Email writing SOP, brand guidelines, hated-task list, and re-engagement skill.
Practise the closing prompt. From this lesson on, it is the last step of every lesson.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.assignment: Done when your decision log exists, holds everything from the earlier lessons, and your AI can read it back to you. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: Help me set up a decision log as a spreadsheet with columns for date, area, decision or SOP, and reason. Add everything we've decided so far. From now on, read it at the start of our work so you don't need retraining. At the end of every chat, add any new decisions and SOPs to it.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

days.title: Teach It to Clean Up Your Inbox
days.why: A tidy inbox means you do not miss the emails that matter.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
days.optionalNote: If you do not want your AI to have access to your email, that is completely fine. Skip this lesson and tap I've completed the lesson and the challenge to move to the next lesson.
steps: Connect your AI to your email (Outlook or Gmail).
Teach it how you like emails filtered and filed, how and when they can be deleted, and where they can be moved.

Set one or two Inbox SOP steps. Examples: 30 days after a BrokerBay showing is done, its request and confirmation emails are archived or deleted. Anything that comes back signed from DocuSign is filed in a folder for that property, checked once a day.
Add your Inbox SOP to your decision log.
If you can't connect it, ask it to give you the text to paste in yourself.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.assignment: Done when your Inbox SOP is saved and you have run it once and checked what moved (or tapped I've completed the lesson and the challenge to skip). Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: I'm going to teach you how I manage my inbox: how I filter and file, what can be deleted and when, and where things should go. For example, 30 days after a BrokerBay showing is done, archive the request and confirmation. Anything signed back from DocuSign goes into that property's folder. Save this as my Inbox SOP. Show me what you'd move or delete before doing it the first time. Then add this Inbox SOP to my decision log.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

days.title: Ask for Reviews
days.why: Happy clients will leave a review if you make it easy and personal.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Teach your AI how you like to request reviews: where (for example Google), your review links, and what you would like to say.
Have it build a text template and an email template, and save them.
When a deal is done, use the short prompt for a text, then ask for the same message by email.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.assignment: Done when you have sent one text and one email requesting a review from a client on a property you have sold this year. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts:
I am going to tell you how I like to ask for reviews: where (for example Google), my review link, and the words I like. Build a text template and an email template and save them.

When I say something like "Hey, I just did a deal with [client]. We just sold 123 Banana Street. I want to send it via text," give me the message with my review link, based on my text template. Do the same when I ask for email. Do not send anything until I approve.
Hey, I just did a deal with [client]. We just sold 123 Banana Street. I want to send it via text. Give me the message with my review link, based on my text template.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

days.title: Share 10 Posts You Like
days.why: Showing real posts is clearer than trying to describe a style.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Find at least 10 social media posts you like the style of.
For each one, take a screenshot and share it with your AI. Screenshots work better than links.
Tell it what you like about them.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.assignment: Done when your AI has created one new version of one of the posts you shared, run through your brand guidelines. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: I am going to share screenshots of at least 10 social posts I like the style of, and say what I like about each. When I have shared them, create one new version of one of those posts for my business, and run it through the brand guidelines we've created. Do not publish it.

days.title: Plan Your Social Media Strategy
days.why: A simple plan you'll actually follow beats random posting.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Decide how many posts you will make each week, and which channels you will use.
Get the sizes: feed posts and carousels are 4:5 (1080 × 1350). Reels and Stories are 9:16 (1080 × 1920).
Brainstorm your first 30 days of posts at that pace.

Stay away from Just Listed, Just Sold and Open House. Mix in neighbourhood events, neighbour highlights, restaurant reviews, things to do on the weekend, Top 10 things to get your home ready for sale, and 5 things that will lose you $10,000 or more in negotiations.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.assignment: Done when you have a written 30-day posting calendar with date, channel, size and topic for each post. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: Help me plan my social media strategy. First ask me how many posts a week I want to make and which channels I'll post on (for example Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn). Then give me the right size for each: 4:5 (1080 × 1350) for feed posts and carousels, and 9:16 (1080 × 1920) for Reels and Stories. Next, brainstorm my first 30 days of posts at that pace, using my brand guide. Avoid Just Listed, Just Sold and Open House posts. Mix in local events, neighbour highlights, restaurant reviews, things to do on the weekend, and helpful seller tips like "Top 10 things to get your home ready for sale" and "5 mistakes that can cost you $10,000 or more in negotiations." Give it to me as a simple calendar table with date, channel, size, topic and a one-line hook. Ask me questions one at a time.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

days.assignment: Done when three posts are finished and approved by you, and any reusable template is saved as an SOP. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: Let's create my first three posts from my social media plan. Help me pick and sharpen my top 3 ideas. I'll share screenshots of posts I like, such as carousels, images and lists. Recreate the style I like using my brand guide: my fonts, colours, headshot and logo. Use the right size for each channel from my plan. Show me one post at a time, and I'll tell you what to change in plain English. If we build a template I'll reuse, save it as an SOP with the steps, sizes and an example.

days.title: Teach It How You Keep Notes
days.why: Once it knows how you take notes, every call, meeting, or pop-by gets logged without you typing.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Create a skill that teaches your AI how you like to keep notes.

If your AI is not connected to your CRM, have it give you the note to paste in.
Test it: dictate a note about a real client (a call, a meeting, or a pop-by) and have it log the note.
Ask it about that client afterwards and check that it pulls the note back.

Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

days.title: Stay in Touch with Past Clients
days.why: Past clients are your best source of repeat and referral business, and your AI can remember the details you cannot.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Build a skill that keeps notes on past clients and tracks home anniversaries, birthdays and kids' names.
Log the note to your CRM, or take the note it gives you to paste in.
Write 5 text options and 5 email options that show you're thinking of them and offering help, for example a snow removal or roofing contact as winter nears.
Test it on one real past client.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.assignment: Done when one past client's dates and details are in your CRM, and you've picked one text or email to send after approving it. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.

I'll tell you about one past client: first names, how we met, the home they bought or sold, the closing date, birthdays, kids' names and anything personal they've shared. Track their home anniversary (closing date) and birthdays. Log these details and dates as a note in my CRM (like Follow Up Boss), or give me the note to paste in if you're not connected. Keep only facts I gave you, and never add ID, banking or mortgage numbers. Do not send anything until I approve.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

days.title: Write Listing Descriptions in Your Top 5
days.why: Your listing description is a top 5, the 5 best reasons to buy this home.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Paste 3 to 5 descriptions you like.
Describe a made-up property.
Edit the draft in plain English.
Save it as the template.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.assignment: Done when your Listing writer skill writes a Top 5 you'd post with only light edits. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts:
Create a skill called Listing writer.

My listing descriptions use a top 5 format. The top 5 is the listing description, not an extra section. It is the 5 best reasons to buy this home.

Here is the format to follow, even before I share examples:

Start with this exact header, on its own line:

Top 5 Reasons You Will Love This Home:

Then write five numbered points, each on its own line, like this: 1) then 2) then 3) then 4) then 5). Use a number, a closing parenthesis, and a space. Do not use bullets, bold labels, or a short title before each point.

Do not add an intro paragraph before the header. Do not add a call to action, a phone number, a brokerage line, or the word REALTOR® in the description.

Each point is usually one sentence, about 30 to 45 words. A little shorter or longer is fine, but keep each point in the 15 to 65 word range, and the whole description around 150 to 250 words (about 200 is typical).

Lead with the strongest reason to buy this home in point 1. That is often the waterfront or lot, a standout garage or shop, a new build or major renovation, the curb appeal, or the lifestyle. Points 2 to 4 cover the supporting reasons, such as the layout and finishes, outdoor living, upgrades and mechanicals, or parking and storage. Point 5 covers location and lifestyle (what is nearby, and drive times only if I give them). End point 5 with the finished square footage in a short factual tag, in this style: 1,420 above grade sq.ft. plus a finished lower level. If I give different floor-area details, use those exact words.

Write in a warm, polished voice, in second person or focused on the home. Do not write in first person. Stack specific facts rather than vague praise. Connecting phrases that fit this style include showcasing, featuring, complemented by, offering, and highlighted by. Use Canadian spelling (neighbourhood, storey, centre, harbour, armour, metre). Do not use em dashes.

Use only the facts I give you. If you need a detail I did not provide, such as a measurement, a year, a distance, or a feature, mark it [CHECK] instead of inventing it. Prefer specific, checkable facts over unsubstantiated superlatives. Do not promise results or use words like guarantee, investment, or "will sell quickly." If you want to say a neighbourhood is sought-after or that something is rare, mark it [CHECK] unless I said it.

If I tell you photos were virtually staged, add this exact final line after point 5:

*Please note some images have been virtually staged to show the potential of the home.

I will paste 3 to 5 listing descriptions I like, so you can tweak the style to match them. If I do not have my own yet, use the format above as the starting point.

Then I will describe a made-up property the way I would at a listing appointment, by voice note, dictation, text, or email. Write one top 5 listing description from those details.

Show me the draft, and I will tell you what to change in plain English. When I am happy, save the final version as the template for this skill.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.sample:
Top 5 Reasons You Will Love This Home:
1) Thoughtfully updated all-brick bungalow showcasing inviting curb appeal and a fully landscaped lot, with a covered front porch and a walkout from the dining area to a private backyard made for relaxing and entertaining
2) Enjoy the ease of main-level living with three bedrooms, two bathrooms, and laundry all on one floor, complemented by an open kitchen and living space with a centre island, quartz counters, and a gas fireplace
3) Extend your living space into the finished lower level, featuring a bright rec room, a fourth bedroom, and a three-piece bathroom, offering a comfortable setup for guests or work-from-home days
4) Practical extras include an attached double-car garage with interior access, a double paved driveway, and a fully fenced backyard with a new deck and garden shed for storage
5) Set on a quiet street close to schools, parks, shops, and the waterfront trail, with the hospital and downtown just a short drive away. 1,420 above grade sq.ft. plus a finished lower level.

days.title: Make the Letter of Opinion Yours
days.why: Turn the ready-made Letter of Opinion template into your own, with your details and your real signature.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Download the Letter of Opinion template from the kit.
Sign your name in dark pen on plain white paper and photograph it in good light.

Run the prompt with the template and your signature photo. Give your AI your full name and your work address, the brokerage office address. Tell it to save both in your business summary and your decision log as your standard agent details.
Check the test PDF: your name, details and signature are in the right spots, and none of the original agent's details are left.
Fix anything in plain English, such as making the signature a bit smaller or moving your phone number under your name.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.
days.assignment: Done when you have a test PDF with your name, details and signature that you'd be proud to send. Before you finish: log every decision you made today in your SOP, or update the SOP it belongs to.
prompts: I'm attaching the Letter of Opinion template from the kit. It's already built, so keep the layout and wording unless I ask for a change. Take out any name, contact details and signature from the original agent, but keep all the formatting exactly as it is. Put my details in their place: my full name is [full name], [title, e.g. REALTOR®], [brokerage], my work address is [brokerage office address], [phone], [email], and I work in [areas]. Save my full name and my work address in my business summary and in my decision log as my standard agent details. I'm also attaching a photo of my signature, signed in dark pen on plain white paper. Turn it into a clean, smooth digital signature with a transparent background and place it on the signature line of the PDF. Show me the finished letter and ask me what I'd like to change. Make my changes, then save it as a skill called Letter of Opinion. Test it on a made-up property at 123 Banana Street, using made-up comparables clearly marked SAMPLE. Nothing is final until I approve it.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

days.title: Practise, then Time a Real Letter
days.why: A past address is a safe rehearsal. The timed letter shows you what a real one costs in minutes.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Practise on a past address: give it the solds and actives you used.
Then draft a real letter and time it.
You approve before anyone sees it.
Before we close, give me every decision we made in this chat. Tell me which SOP each one belongs in, update that SOP if it already exists, or give me new rows for my decision log.

days.title: Read an Offer: The Coles Notes
days.why: Offers are long. Your client needs the key points, fast and clearly.
days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: Teach your AI how to read an Agreement of Purchase and Sale (APS), the contract used to buy a home in Ontario.
Give it some mock signbacks so it gets a feel for what they look like. A signback is the offer sent back with changes.
Teach it to read the Confirmation of Acceptance so it knows when an offer has been accepted.
Give it guidelines on what is relevant to share with a client (price, deposit, conditions and their dates, closing date, inclusions and exclusions) so it does not repeat the whole agreement.
Save it as a skill.

days.title: Prep Your Listing Appointment Paperwork

days.minutes: 15 to 30 minutes, longer if you go deeper
steps: The RECO Information Guide and the Form 200 listing agreement are in your kit. In WEBForms (the online system for Ontario real estate forms), build your blank masters yourself from those files: the RECO guide, and a listing agreement with your standard Schedule A (the extra page of terms on the listing agreement), saved as editable PDFs.
Pre-fill your standard terms in the master: commission 5% total with 2.5% to the co-operating brokerage, and a 60-day holdover (the period after the listing ends when a commission can still be owed).
Teach your AI to turn a GeoWarehouse report into a ready-to-fill details sheet: owner names, address and property details, postal code checked on Google, listing start date and number of days.
Save it as a skill.
